rounds.fact: LinkedIn launched in 2003 out of a founder's living room. By 2005 it was already leaning into the dense, spreadsheet-like profile layout that professional networking sites still use.
Vine's entire format was built around exactly 6-second looping videos, a constraint that produced its own distinct style of comedy before Twitter shut the app down in 2017.
Encyclopedia Britannica put its entire encyclopedia online for free in 1999, a bold bet that ad revenue could replace its centuries-old subscription business, before pulling back a year later.
StumbleUpon's whole concept was a browser button that took you to a random, algorithm-picked website matching your interests, a discovery model that faded as social feeds took over that role.
Addicting Games grew rapidly during the mid-2000s Flash gaming boom, hosting thousands of free browser games at a time when installing a game usually still meant buying a physical disc.
